neighbours.label: real-estate listing context, at the modifier just before the property noun ('two-storey ▮', 'a brand new ▮'), where 'property' is the expected next word
fire: The developer is selling a brand new two-storey townhouse close to the marina.
This charming three-bedroom cottage sits on a quiet lane near the village centre.
Buyers looking for a newly built detached home will like this gated estate.
The agency has listed several two-storey villas with private pools on the coast.
We are pleased to offer for sale this spacious ground-floor apartment with a terrace.
A collection of brand new lodges is now available for holiday letting.
The landlord is renting out a fully furnished two-bedroom flat near the station.
Rising demand pushed up the value of residential homes across the region.
quiet: The dealer is selling a brand new two-seater sports car close to the marina.
This charming three-act comedy opens on a quiet evening at the village theatre.
Readers looking for a newly published detective novel will like this series.
The museum has shown several two-metre sculptures with bronze bases on the lawn.
We are pleased to offer for hire this spacious twelve-seat minibus with a driver.
A collection of brand new poems is now available for school reading.
The captain is hiring a fully trained two-man crew near the harbour.
Rising demand pushed up the price of fresh vegetables across the region.

notes: Card: ' new', ' the', ' two', ' low', ' higher' in property and holiday-let text; the output promotes ' property' / ' properties' in every casing. Probes: 'a brand new two-storey villa' 0.58, 'three-bedroom detached house has … a' 0.38, 'luxury villas' 0.33, 'two flats' 0.26; 'fall of the share price' 0.23, 'brand new car' 0.09, 'brand new phone' 0.03. Activations are moderate, so the 0.20 median is not safe. Near misses keep the modifiers outside real estate.
